outcome: Indications for cesarean section (abnormal fetal monitoring, obstructed labor)
cohort: The study included 33,785 nulliparous women with singleton livebirth pregnancies, aged 14 to 40+ years, who delivered at a university maternity over a 24.5-year period.
finding: Vaginal births without obstetrical assistance among primiparas occurred more frequently at younger maternal ages, showing a consistent negative linear trend as age increased.
mod_finding: Younger primiparous women (14-15 years) exhibited significantly higher rates of unassisted vaginal deliveries (91%) and lower rates of cesarean sections (9%) and operative vaginal deliveries (12.1%) compared to older counterparts (>=40 years).
